title: Calibration run hygiene: scheduler throttles, artifact quarantine, and scoped permission guardrails
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Calibration runs for quantization (FP8/INT8) are growing in number and size as teams onboard more models and sweep configurations. This creates operational issues: noisy long-running runs consume cluster capacity, stale artifacts accumulate, and permissions are too coarse (full project access) which increases blast radius for accidental promotion or download of calibration artifacts.

Goal: Ship a set of console features and orchestration rules that introduce: 1) scheduler throttles and priority classes for calibration jobs, 2) an artifact quarantine + TTL hygiene policy for intermediate snapshots and signed artifacts, and 3) scoped role-based access controls for run-level artifact access (read-only consumer vs. promotion/restore). The UX should make trade-offs visible (cost vs. accuracy) and provide safe defaults for teams onboarding calibration sweeps.
background: Redwood's calibration pipeline produces multiple artifacts per run: raw activation dumps, calibration statistics, quant profiles (v1/v2), signed promoted artifacts, and ephemeral checkpoints for long sweeps. Currently, runs are queued FIFO with a simple per-team concurrency cap; artifacts are retained indefinitely until a manual cleanup. Audit logs show multiple incidents where stale promoted artifacts caused regressions in serving. Customers requesting stricter data governance and platform teams asking for predictable cluster capacity during peak batch runs.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler supports at least three priority classes (low=batch, default=interactive, high=blocking) that owners can set per-run
Admin policy allows per-project concurrency caps and global ramp-down during infra maintenance
Artifact lifecycle policy UI that sets TTLs for snapshots and raw activations with an explicit quarantine state for signed artifacts awaiting promotion
RBAC rules that create two new roles: calibration-viewer (read-only access to run metadata/artifacts) and calibration-operator (can promote artifacts and trigger restores)
Console shows estimated storage and compute cost per run before launch
End-to-end e2e test coverage for scheduling priority and artifact TTL enforcement
Documentation pages and migration guide for teams with >50 active runs
implementation_notes: Work will be split across: backend scheduler changes (open-source runtime could be updated to accept priority hints), artifact-service GC hooks, and console UI for run creation and artifact policy. Key infra tasks: add priority metadata to job protobufs, implement priority preemption policy, extend artifact metadata with 'quarantine_until' and 'signed_by' fields, and wire new RBAC checks into artifact promotion APIs. We will provide an experimental opt-in toggle for teams to use strict retention for 30 days before making it default.
design_considerations: Defaults should favor safety: low priority for broad sweeps, explicit high priority only for labeled 'blocking' experiments
Quarantine should prevent automated promotion until a review checkbox is toggled to avoid accidental rollouts
UI should surface trade-offs: if TTL < 7 days, warn that re-running sweep may be required for future model versions
RBAC must be role-scoped to tenant/project and compatible with existing SSO groups
open_questions: Should preemption kill low-priority runs immediately or checkpoint and reschedule?
What is the canonical retention tiers (7d/30d/90d/forever) and do we support custom TTLs?
How do we surface cost estimates reliably for long-running batches with variable token counts?
Do we need a separate approval workflow for cross-team artifact promotion?
decisions: Use soft preemption: checkpoint low-priority runs every 15 minutes and allow resumption instead of hard kill
Ship three retention tiers (30d default for intermediate snapshots, 90d for promoted artifacts, manual for 'archive')
Introduce two roles (calibration-viewer, calibration-operator) rather than per-tenant custom roles in first iteration
Cost estimate to show conservative upper bound and historical median to avoid under-promising
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Preemption could increase total run time and cost. Mitigation: soft preemption with checkpointing to avoid wasted compute.
Risk: RBAC changes might break existing automation. Mitigation: provide migration script and deprecation window with audit logs for blocked actions.
Risk: Aggressive TTL deletes artifacts needed for future audits. Mitigation: quarantine+promote workflow and 'archive' manual option for legal holds.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement scheduler priority and soft preemption for 10 internal teams (2 weeks). Phase 2: add artifact TTL UI and backend GC with a 30-day trial on opt-in projects (3 weeks). Phase 3: add RBAC roles and migration tooling, then flip default retention to 30d for new projects after 30-day notice (4 weeks). Each phase includes post-launch monitoring dashboard and rollback plan.
monitoring_and_slo: New metrics to add: run.priority_distribution, preemption.count, artifact.gc.deleted_per_hour, artifact.quarantine_wait_time, permission.denied_count. SLO: 99% of high-priority runs start within X minutes; artifact GC should complete deletions within 1 hour of TTL expiry for 95% of objects.
qa_steps: Create test job with low priority and verify checkpoint/resume behavior under induced load
Verify TTL deletion and quarantine state with unit tests and staged GC run
Test promotion API with calibration-viewer role (should fail) and calibration-operator role (should succeed)
Simulate maintenance window and confirm global ramp-down respects project concurrency caps
migration_notes: Existing projects will be given a default migration policy (retain promoted artifacts for 90d, snapshots 30d). We will email project owners and surface in-console banner with a 'migrate now' button that runs a dry-run showing which artifacts would be deleted. There will be a one-month grace period before enforcement.
